question: How many chemical elements are named after Ytterby, a small village near Stockholm?
answer: Four: yttrium, ytterbium, terbium and erbium all take their names from Ytterby, whose quarry produced unusual rocks that chemists kept splitting into new elements. Kean calls it the Galapagos of the periodic table: one small place that taught chemists a great deal about a whole family of elements.
move: Small places can matter enormously; check before assuming fame follows size.
trap: 'One': it seems generous for any village to get even one.
simply: One Swedish village had a quarry full of strange rocks. Four elements found in them are named after it.
why: It shows how discovery clusters: one rich source, studied closely, can yield far more than its size suggests.
reference: Sam Kean, The Disappearing Spoon (Little, Brown, 2010), ch. 3
